title: Grateful Dead Live at Civic Auditorium on 1969-01-17
lineage: CD -> Samplitude Professional v10.02 -> Cool Edit Pro v2.0 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: A soundboard capture of the January 17 1969 show delivers a high‑energy performance with a smoking Dark Star, stellar Eleven and tight drumming, though the tempo feels a touch slow.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean soundboard mix that lets Jerry’s god‑like guitar tone and Mickey’s punchy bass drum shine, despite occasional cuts and an overly prominent kick. Musically the show shines – Dark Star, The Eleven, St. Stephen and Death Don't Have No Mercy are highlighted, while the first Cosmic Charlie and a sluggish Love Light sit lower in the set. Overall it’s a transcendent early‑’69 performance that most fans rate as essential listening.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 5‑star praising the musical execution and the clean soundboard recording; only minor technical quirks (bass drum level, a cut in St. Stephen) keep it from perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean mix with clear guitar and vocal detail; bass drum is prominent but not distracting for most listeners. A brief cut in the middle of St. Stephen is noted, and pitch‑correction has been applied to restore original tempo/pitch.

poor_songs: Turn on Your Love Light (slow tempo)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The early‑’69 set flows tightly, with Dark Star anchoring the performance and seamless transitions into The Eleven and other classics; the energy builds despite a few slower moments.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly called ‘god‑like’; his guitar tone, phrasing and improvisational flow are praised as phenomenal.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass riffs are highlighted on Cosmic Charlie and the prominent bass drum mix lets Phil’s lines shine; reviewers note his “fingerprints” on the music.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten (TC) is present but his keyboards are described as over‑thought and not prominent in the mix; some miss Pigpen’s soulful style.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s bass drum is louder than usual but generally praised; snare drums sound crisp and the overall drum work is tight.
